title: The Second Summer
premise: Sable Okafor, a wedding planner who stopped believing in love after her own engagement collapsed twelve years ago, agrees to a fake date with Theo Marchetti to survive her family's reunion — but the pretend romance turns real by dessert. When her estranged grandmother dies and leaves Sable a controlling share of the family's coastal resort, she inherits not just property but a buried injustice: proof that her late father was cheated out of his stake decades ago. As relatives close ranks and Theo — the resort's lawyer, hired to keep the will quiet — is revealed as both ally and deceiver, Sable must choose between the safe life she built and the justice her father never got. She forgives herself for walking away all those years ago, exposes the truth at the resort's centennial gala, and chooses Theo not as an escape from her past but as a partner in what comes next.
about_author: Sebastian Villalobos is a former hospitality manager who spent a decade planning weddings on the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction full-time. He writes stories about people who rebuild themselves out of the wreckage of family, money, and almost-love.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Twelve years after fleeing her broken engagement, Sable runs a meticulous wedding-planning business built on other people's joy and her own emotional distance. A letter summons her to the Okafor family reunion at the crumbling seaside resort her grandmother still owns. Beat: controlled loneliness cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: The Terms of the Deal
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Dreading questions about her love life, Sable strikes a bargain with Theo Marchetti, a charming stranger at the resort bar who claims he needs a plus-one too. They invent a meet-cute, rehearse their story over cheap wine, and agree: no real feelings, one weekend only. Beat: playful complicity masking mutual guardedness.

chapters.title: Reunion
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The fake couple performs flawlessly through the reunion's first day — until Sable's aunt Delia recognizes Theo as the lawyer whose firm has been quietly handling the family's affairs for years. Dessert arrives with a hand on Sable's knee that neither of them planned. Beat: the performance becoming dangerously real.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Grandmother Ijeoma, sharp-tongued and failing, takes a liking to Theo and lets slip that she's changing her will — and that she knows what was done to Sable's father. Theo, bound by client confidentiality to Delia's faction, says nothing. Beat: guilt taking root beneath charm.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ijeoma dies suddenly. The will names Sable majority owner of the resort — to the family's open fury — along with a locked box of her father's old documents. Reading her father's letters, Sable learns he was bought out for pennies before his death. Beat: grief transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: Paper Trails
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sable digs into the records; Theo, torn between his firm and his feelings, secretly pulls the original sale contracts. They discover Delia and her husband engineered the buyout with forged signatures. Working together by night, pretending neutrality by day, they cross a line neither can uncross. Beat: intimacy forged in shared secrets.

chapters.title: Everything Except the Truth
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Delia confronts Theo with evidence of his leaks and offers him partnership if he hands over Sable's findings. Cornered, he lies to Sable about where he was that night — and she finds Delia's offer letter in his coat. Beat: betrayal repeating the oldest wound Sable has.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Devastated, Sable nearly signs the resort away and walks back to her small safe life. Instead she rereads her father's last letter — telling her to live bravely, not safely — and admits she left Theo because leaving is what she does. She forgives the woman in the mirror. Beat: the internal climax.

chapters.title: Centennial Gala
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the resort's hundredth-anniversary gala, Sable takes the stage and presents the forged documents to the assembled family and guests. Delia's counterattack collapses when Ijeoma's lawyer produces a sealed affidavit the grandmother prepared before dying. Theo publicly resigns from his firm and stands beside Sable, unasked. Beat: external climax — justice outside the courtroom.

chapters.title: The Second Summer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Months later, the resort reopens under Sable's stewardship, its first event a small wedding she plans — and believes in — for the first time in twelve years. On the same beach where her father once proposed to her mother, Theo asks nothing except to stay. She says yes. Beat: earned resolution, love chosen freely.
